PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.form: CES_end_to_end = P(required evidence survives the compressor) x P(S2 succeeds | it survived)
PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.rule: For ANY compression mechanism, never report conditional selector performance alone. Always pair coverage after compression with conditional performance, and report the end-to-end composition.
PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.scope: applies to G1_TYPED_PATH, G2, and every future compression or traversal mechanism
PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.why: B4 proved conditional metrics can lie. P2 at M=25 posted 0.785 selected-CES-given-working at cal_3000 -- the best single number in the table -- while having discarded half the required evidence before S2 ever saw it. End-to-end it merely matched plain k=50. The conditional metric RISES as a compressor throws evidence away, so reporting it alone rewards exactly the failure it should expose.

architecture: Question -> identity resolution -> SMALL global seed retrieval -> runtime evidence graph -> bounded relation-aware expansion -> working candidate set -> UNCHANGED S2 -> 6 records -> (HRM later)
edge_construction_rule: every edge must be derivable from visible evidence text or an existing runtime parser
eventual_division_of_labour: dense/BM25 gets into the right neighbourhood; the graph moves through it; S2 decides what enters working memory; HRM reasons over the six records; an executive later decides whether another traversal is worth performing.
forbidden_absolutely: the evaluator proof graph in any form

graph_scope_deliberately_small.construction: record -> entity extraction -> entities -> relation extraction -> typed edges, all from visible text via runtime parsers.
graph_scope_deliberately_small.ephemeral_not_persistent: Build the graph from the current corpus/evidence representation per run. No persistent memory substrate yet.
graph_scope_deliberately_small.hop_limit: 1-2 hops in G1. No arbitrary graph walks.

G1_TYPED_PATH.pipeline: C2 expanded -> relation-typed path scorer -> bounded set -> S2
G1_TYPED_PATH.role: CHEAP DIAGNOSTIC, run BEFORE declaring graph necessity
G1_TYPED_PATH.rule: rank candidates by whether they form subject -> bridge -> target relation using only observable content: canonical subject, parsed target relation, runtime-visible one-hop entity
G1_TYPED_PATH.why_it_matters: If this trivial deterministic path representation closes most of P3 - P2, then a graph substrate is not yet needed. If it does not, the graph earns its complexity. One frozen arm, NOT a tuning sprint.

G1_coarse.pipeline: C2 expanded -> P2 coarse compressor -> S2
G1_coarse.role: failed-compressor baseline, the floor to beat

G2_graph.pipeline: seed retrieval -> runtime graph expansion -> bounded set -> S2

leakage_enforcement: an executable test of the same kind used around selector_v2: strip docstrings and comments, then assert no executable statement references any forbidden field. The evaluator graph and the runtime graph must remain completely separate objects.

measured_opportunity.meaning: That gap is what better structural discrimination is worth, with HRM, S2 and the six-record packet all unchanged. It is the budget any new middle layer must earn.

no_heuristic_grid: The comparison is coarse P2 vs typed-path vs graph traversal vs oracle P3. No weight sweeps.
objective: Recover the structural discrimination P3 demonstrated, using ONLY runtime-observable relationships, while keeping the candidate set presented to S2 bounded.

stack_assessment.retriever_reachability: solved enough for now; zero unranked records at any scale

success_condition: G2 must obtain the best of both failed regimes: P1's availability WITH P2's low pressure. Anything less is one of the two known failures wearing a new mechanism.

target_regime.note: A graph that returns 250 candidates has not solved the problem. Efficiency is part of the hypothesis, not a footnote.

the_question_the_graph_answers: Given where I am in memory, which structurally relevant neighbourhood should I inspect next?

three_regimes_isolated_by_b4.conclusion: The architecture works IF the middle layer can distinguish structurally useful evidence. That is a discrimination problem, not a retrieval or selector problem.

why_not_another_flat_heuristic: P2's rule was 'keep what looks structurally plausible, then trust retrieval rank' -- and bridge retrieval rank is the known weak signal, so it reduced the pool while preserving the retriever's original mistake. Adding weights (subject +2, relation +3, one-hop +4, score x0.7) would be hand-tuned graph reasoning disguised as a scoring heuristic. Rejected on that basis, not on performance.
